Up for a Vote

Know a regional food we missed, or the place that does it best? Nominate it. Nothing goes on the map automatically: it has to earn the votes first, then it gets a final review. Think somebody's got it wrong? Start a food fight.

  1. Nominate itMembers name the food or place, the region, and why it belongs.
  2. Vote it up or down▲ Belongs or ▼ Not from here. It shows here and on its region page, not on the map. 60 days to reach the bar.
  3. Hit the bar25 net votes (ups minus downs) for a regional food, 15 for a place to get it.
  4. Editor's callWe check that it's real, regional and not a duplicate, and read both sides of any food fight. Then it's added, or "Not this time" with a reason.

The board

Prototype demo: vote, pick sides and start food fights. It all resets when you reload, and sample counts start at zero at launch.

🔥 What's a food fight?When locals don't agree

Think it's really from somewhere else, or not regional at all? Hit Food fight and say where it's from. Once 5 members push back, or the downs get close to the ups, the card gets the Food Fight badge and shows both sides.

Some fights are just for fun, like who makes the best riggies. Pick a team.

The fine print

  • One vote per member: up or down, not both. Your own nomination doesn't count toward the bar.
  • Down votes count. The bar is net votes, so a pile of "Not from here" holds it back.
  • Food fights inform the call. The editor sees every side before deciding, and can settle a fight for good.
  • Keep it friendly. Argue about the food, not the people. Personal attacks get removed.
  • Businesses can't vote for themselves. Owners list their place through Get on the Trail instead.
  • Locals count. Votes from members who live in the region are shown separately.
  • Duplicates get merged and their votes combined.
  • Reaching the bar earns a review, not a guaranteed spot. Missed the bar? It comes off after 60 days and can be nominated again in six months.
